To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the delay of feedback in CAI is an effective instructional strategy that is worth investigating further.

1) the delay of feedback in a computer-based program for the teaching of sex knowledge resulted in significantly better retention than the immediate feedback condition and the no feedback condition, 2) there was no significant difference in retention between the immediate feedback and the no feedback conditions, and 3) the no feedback condition was significantly more difficult for the students than the other two conditions, but the difference between the immediate feedback condition was not significant.
(1) delayed feedback was more effective than immediate feedback; and (2) the effect of delayed feedback was more pronounced when the delay was longer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of delayed feedback on learning and retention in a computer-assisted instructional task.
the effect of feedback delay in a CAI program.
the effects of delay of informational feedback on learning and retention in a computer-assisted instructional task.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the retention and delay of feedback in CAI is an area which needs further research, particularly in the area of retention and the effects of different delay intervals on the retention of the material.
the delay of feedback in a CAI task is beneficial to retention and recall.

a 15-second feedback delay in computer-assisted instruction results in significantly better retention of material than immediate feedback, but that immediate feedback is better than feedback delayed until after a series of responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
feedback delay is not a negative aspect of computer-assisted instruction.
the use of delayed feedback, especially delayed feedback after a set of responses, may have some advantages over immediate feedback in a programmed instructional task.
the use of a delay in the feedback condition in a CAI program is an effective method of increasing retention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
delayed feedback can be more effective in retention and learning than immediate feedback.
students who receive feedback on a 15-second interval perform significantly better on a delayed retention test than those who received feedback immediately after each response.
the delay of feedback can be used as a strategy to increase retention of information in CAI tasks.
